brief: A kitchen herb planter: two or three bins on a base, filled with soil and planted with basil and thyme.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Two or three bins on a base
requirements.evidence: 3 full-depth bins placed: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full on 3 Hex bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) arranged as compact triangular cluster. check_build clear.
fillSoil succeeded for all three bins via fill_and_plant (soil in each bin, no warnings).
Basil planted in two bins: prop:1 basil-young in bin:0,0,0 and prop:3 basil-harvest in bin:1,0,0 — both visible in look views.
Thyme planted in remaining bin: prop:2 thyme-young in bin:0,1,0 — visible in look views alongside basil.

finish.summary: Built compact kitchen herb planter with 3 full-depth bins on 3 Hex bases in triangular layout. All bins filled with soil; planted with basil (young + harvest stages) and thyme (young) to satisfy both herbs. House rules applied (capOpenFaces, lockJoints) and check_build clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your herb planter is on the way — I'll get its bins and fresh basil going.
